title: $2.56 Million in Stock — or $1,499? The Fake Proof Behind Fyre Festival

lines.say: Investors wanted to know Billy McFarland could back his promises. Prosecutors said he showed them proof.
An altered brokerage statement showing two point five six million dollars in stock. He actually owned one thousand four hundred ninety-nine dollars' worth.
lines.show: An altered brokerage statement showing $2.56 million in stock. He actually owned $1,499 worth.

lines.say: A banker's email approving a three million dollar loan. The banker never sent it.
lines.show: A banker's email approving a $3 million loan. The banker never sent it.

lines.say: And the sale of his earlier company, Magnises, for about forty million dollars, to Saddleback Media. There was no sale.
lines.show: And the sale of his earlier company, Magnises, for about $40 million, to Saddleback Media. There was no sale.

lines.say: One document bore the electronic signature of Saddleback's president, a G. Smythe. Prosecutors said that person does not exist.
lines.show: One document bore the electronic signature of Saddleback's president, a "G. Smythe." Prosecutors said that person does not exist.

lines.say: In July two thousand eighteen, he admitted the S.E.C.'s allegations.
lines.show: In July 2018, he admitted the SEC's allegations.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
